In May of this year, Lux Optics launched the all-new iPhone professional camera app Halide Mark III. Today, Halide delivers its first update, designed specifically for the iPhone 18 Pro while bringing new features to all iPhone photography enthusiasts.

At its core, Halide Mark III is on a mission to help iPhone users capture better photos.

Highlights include a redesigned camera interface, an all-new photo editor, and the Halide Looks filter feature that gives your work a distinctive style.

Halide 3.1, released in July, builds on that foundation with additional Halide Looks filters and other features.

  • Halide Mark III professional camera app debuts with three major photography upgrades
  • Halide 3.1 adds perspective correction, dedicated RAW capture, and more

Now Halide 3.2 is officially here, offering full support for the upgraded iPhone 18 Pro camera system.

Aperture Priority mode

The new version introduces Aperture Priority mode, building on Halide's ability to select any aperture value from ƒ/1.48 to ƒ/4.0.

(The built-in Camera app supports an automatic variable aperture mode, with manual selection available at ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, or ƒ/4.0.)

The Aperture Priority mode Halide 3.2 brings to the iPhone 18 Pro lets you set a target aperture value, after which Halide automatically adjusts shutter speed and ISO based on the shooting scene.

Meanwhile, full Manual mode also supports direct ISO adjustment.

New Halide Looks filters: dawn and quicksilver

In addition, Halide 3.2 adds two new filters for all iPhone models: dawn and quicksilver.

dawn "brings cinematic warm tones to midtones and highlights, with soft, richly layered shadows"; quicksilver offers "high contrast paired with low-saturation colors, inspired by silver-halide preservation and development processes".

Finally, Halide 3.2 adds a 16:9 shooting aspect ratio mode.

Halide Mark III is available for a one-time purchase of US$69.99, while subscribers can enjoy the new app for US$19.99 per year.
